faqs.question: How long does ceramic coating last?
faqs.answer: A professionally applied ceramic coating typically lasts 3–5 years with proper maintenance. Some premium coatings we apply are rated for 7+ years. Longevity depends on the product tier, how thorough the prep was, and how you maintain the vehicle afterward. We'll walk you through everything at pickup.

We won't coat over defects, which is why some shops do and their results don't last.

faqs.question: What's the difference between ceramic coating and wax?
faqs.answer: Wax sits on top of your paint and washes away within weeks. Ceramic coating chemically bonds to the clear coat, creating a permanent hydrophobic layer that repels water, blocks UV radiation, and resists chemical contamination from bird droppings, road salt, and tree sap. It lasts years — not weeks.

faqs.question: Can I wash my car after ceramic coating?
faqs.answer: You should avoid water contact for 5–7 days after application while the coating fully cures. After that, washing becomes easier — the hydrophobic surface causes water and dirt to slide right off. We'll give you a detailed aftercare sheet when you pick up the vehicle.

faqs.question: When's the best time to undercoat?
faqs.answer: The best time is when the vehicle is new, before any salt exposure — ideally before the first winter. If the vehicle is used, undercoating is still effective as long as the rust hasn't progressed to structural damage. We do undercoating year-round — fall and spring are popular, but any time works.

faqs.question: Rubberized vs. oil-based — which is better?
faqs.answer: Both serve different purposes and work best together. Rubberized undercoating is ideal for flat exposed surfaces — it creates a thick, permanent rubber barrier. Oil-based (fluid film) penetrates into seams, crevices, and frame cavities that rubber can't reach. Many customers opt for both for maximum protection. We'll recommend the right approach for your vehicle.

faqs.question: Can you undercoat a vehicle that already has rust?
faqs.answer: Yes. For surface and minor pitting rust, we apply a rust neutralizer that converts active rust into a stable compound, then coat over it. More significant rust requires mechanical prep first. We inspect the vehicle and quote any additional prep work before starting — you'll never be surprised by charges.

faqs.question: Is dealer undercoating worth it?
faqs.answer: Dealer undercoating is typically a thin spray applied in minutes — it's primarily a profit center for the dealer, not a serious rust protection solution. Professional undercoating from Capital Upfitters uses proper materials, applied with the right equipment, by specialists who do this every day. We see customers regularly who had dealer coating fail within two years. Don't waste the money — do it right.

faqs.answer: Yes — any suspension modification that changes the front suspension geometry requires a fresh alignment. We either handle alignment in-house or coordinate with our alignment partner so you're not driving away with a crooked truck.

faqs.question: Will a lift kit affect my warranty?
faqs.answer: Lift kits installed by certified professionals using quality parts won't void your powertrain warranty under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act. However, if a lift-related component causes a failure, that component's coverage may be affected. We use quality branded kits (ReadyLIFT, Rough Country, BDS) to minimize this risk.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a leveling kit and a lift kit?
faqs.answer: A leveling kit only raises the front end to match the rear height — typically 1.5″–3″ of lift. A lift kit raises the entire vehicle, front and rear, for true additional ground clearance. Leveling kits are simpler, cheaper, and faster to install. Lift kits offer more capability but require more parts and labor.

faqs.question: Can I fit 35″ tires with a leveling kit?
faqs.answer: Usually no — leveling kits typically allow 33″ tires on full-size trucks. For 35s, you generally need 3″–4″ of lift (or more on some trucks). We'll confirm what your specific truck can fit at each lift level before you commit.

faqs.question: How long does the install take?
faqs.body: Most installs take 2–3 hours from drop-off to pickup. We recommend scheduling a morning appointment so your truck is ready by early afternoon. Same-day service is typically available.

faqs.question: What sets Patriot Liner apart?
faqs.body: While many spray-on bedliner brands exist, many share similar core chemistry. Patriot Liner is engineered with a refined polyurea formulation that delivers a deeper, richer black finish and enhanced UV resistance and durability (lab proven). Its advanced application characteristics allow it to lay down smoother and more consistently, creating a clean, uniform finish that stands out. Combined with a lifetime warranty, it's built for customers who want both durability and a premium look.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.body: Pricing starts at $575 for compact trucks (up to 5ft bed), $595 for standard (up to 6.5ft), $635 for HD trucks, and $675 for long 8ft beds. Add +$200 for the Premium UV+ formula upgrade. All prices plus tax. Request installed pricing online or call us at (301) 304-1419.

faqs.question: Do you do custom colors?
faqs.body: Yes. While black is the standard color, Patriot Liner is available in custom colors. Custom color requests may require additional lead time. Contact us to discuss your options before booking.

faqs.question: Can you spray liner something besides a truck bed?
faqs.body: Yes — Patriot Liner bonds to metal, wood, concrete, and fiberglass. We regularly coat trailer beds, van floors, boat gunwales, garage floors, steps, and commercial vehicle cargo areas. Call us and describe your surface — if it can be prepped properly, we can coat it.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a camper shell and a tonneau cover?
faqs.body: A camper shell (also called a truck cap or topper) is a full enclosure that sits on top of your bed rails, fully enclosing your cargo area. A tonneau cover is a flat panel that covers only the bed opening. Shells offer much more security, weather protection, and usable vertical space.

faqs.question: Can you match my truck's color?
faqs.body: Yes — Ranch shells are available in factory color-match finishes for Ford, RAM, Chevrolet/GMC, Toyota, and Nissan. We use your truck's color code to order the exact match.

faqs.question: How long does installation take?
faqs.body: Most installs are same-day or next-day. The shell bolts to your bed rails with a weatherstrip seal — installation takes about 1–2 hours.

faqs.question: Do you have models in stock?
faqs.body: We keep popular models in stock for the most common truck sizes. Call (301) 304-1419 to check availability for your specific truck.

faqs.question: Can I add interior lighting or a bed liner under the shell?
faqs.body: Yes — we recommend adding a Patriot Liner spray-on bedliner when installing a shell. Interior lighting, bed slides, and van shelving can also be added for a complete mobile workspace setup.

faqs.question: How long does ceramic coating last?
faqs.body: A professionally applied ceramic coating typically lasts 3–5 years with proper maintenance. Some premium coatings we apply are rated for 7+ years. Longevity depends on the product tier, how thorough the prep was, and how you maintain the vehicle afterward. We'll walk you through everything at pickup.

faqs.question: Is prep work included in the price?
faqs.body: Surface decontamination is included in all pricing. Paint correction (polishing out swirls, scratches, and oxidation) is quoted separately based on the paint's actual condition — we assess before we quote. We won't coat over defects, which is why some shops do and their results don't last.

faqs.question: What's the difference between ceramic coating and wax?
faqs.body: Wax sits on top of your paint and washes away within weeks. Ceramic coating chemically bonds to the clear coat, creating a permanent hydrophobic layer that repels water, blocks UV radiation, and resists chemical contamination from bird droppings, road salt, and tree sap. It lasts years — not weeks.

faqs.question: Can I wash my car after ceramic coating?
faqs.body: You should avoid water contact for 5–7 days after application while the coating fully cures. After that, washing becomes easier — the hydrophobic surface causes water and dirt to slide right off. We'll give you a detailed aftercare sheet when you pick up the vehicle.

faqs.question: Will fender flares affect my truck's aerodynamics?
faqs.body: OE-style fender flares have minimal aerodynamic impact since they follow the factory body contour. Cut-out/wide-body flares have a slightly larger profile but the difference in fuel economy is negligible for most drivers.

faqs.question: Do grille guards affect airbag deployment?
faqs.body: Quality grille guards from reputable brands (Go Rhino, Ranch Hand, Westin) are engineered to not interfere with factory crash sensors or airbag deployment. We only install brands that meet or exceed these standards.

faqs.question: Can I add a winch to an aftermarket bumper?
faqs.body: Most Ranch Hand and Fab Fours front bumpers are winch-ready with a built-in receiver. WARN and Superwinch are common pairings. Ask us about the full setup when requesting a quote.

faqs.question: Do you install WeatherTech products?
faqs.body: Yes — we install WeatherTech mud flaps and Husky Liners splash guards. These are precision-fit laser-measured products that look factory installed and require professional installation to seat correctly.

faqs.question: What is a Stealth Hitch?
faqs.body: A Stealth Hitch is a vehicle-specific hidden receiver hitch that tucks completely out of sight when not in use — no visible tube hanging below your bumper. They're designed for luxury SUVs and vehicles where aesthetics matter. Stealth Hitches start at $1,000 for parts and labor and are available for most popular SUV models.

faqs.question: Will a hitch void my warranty?
faqs.body: In most cases, no. The Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act protects you — a dealer cannot void your warranty simply because an aftermarket part was installed. We use OEM-style installation methods that don't compromise your frame or electrical system. If your dealer threatens this, they're misinformed about the law.

faqs.question: How long does hitch installation take?
faqs.body: Most standard hitch installations take 2–3 hours. Stealth Hitch installs can take 3–4 hours depending on vehicle complexity. We'll confirm your estimated completion time when you schedule — same-day service is available most days.

faqs.question: Do you install wiring harnesses?
faqs.body: Yes. We install 4-pin flat and 7-pin round trailer wiring harnesses. We also install electric brake controllers for trailers with brakes. Add this to your hitch install appointment and we'll wire everything in a single visit.

faqs.question: Do you install 5th wheel hitches and gooseneck systems?
faqs.body: Yes — we install 5th wheel hitches, gooseneck conversion balls, brake controllers, and weight distribution systems. These are all custom-fit to your specific truck and trailer configuration. Call us or submit a quote with your truck year/make/model and what you plan to tow.

faqs.question: What surfaces can you coat?
faqs.body: Nearly any substrate — steel, aluminum, concrete, wood, fiberglass, and existing coated surfaces with proper preparation. We coat vehicle cargo floors, truck beds, trailer interiors, cargo van floors, industrial floors, dock ramps, structural steel, containment areas, and facility surfaces.

faqs.question: Do you offer mobile on-site application?
faqs.body: Yes — our mobile application unit serves job sites, fleet yards, government facilities, and industrial locations throughout the DMV region. For large-scale fleet programs or facility work, we bring the equipment to you. Contact us to discuss scope and scheduling.

faqs.question: Do I need a relay for an LED light bar?
faqs.body: Yes — for any high-draw LED light bar (over 50W), a proper relay and fuse setup is required. This protects your factory wiring and ensures the light gets full voltage. We include proper relay wiring on all our light bar installs.

faqs.question: Are LED light bars legal to use on public roads in Maryland?
faqs.body: Most LED light bars are DOT-legal for off-road use only when mounted on roof or bumper. Some SAE-compliant driving/fog lights are street-legal. We'll advise on compliance during the consultation and mark non-street-legal lights appropriately.

faqs.question: Can you wire lights to work with my factory fog light switch?
faqs.body: Yes — on many trucks we can integrate new LED lights to switch on with your factory fog light controls. Other setups use a clean, hidden switch panel. We'll confirm what's possible for your specific truck.

faqs.question: Do you do LED upgrades for commercial fleets?
faqs.body: Yes — fleet lighting is a specialty. We can spec and install standardized packages across multiple vehicles, maintain fleet records, and work with government procurement requirements. Call us for fleet pricing.

faqs.question: Do you offer detailing at your shop?
faqs.body: No — our detailing service is 100% mobile. Our crew comes to your home, office, or fleet yard. This keeps your schedule flexible and eliminates any need to drop off your vehicle.

faqs.question: How long does each package take?
faqs.body: Interior Basic: approximately 1–1.5 hours. Interior Complete: 2–3 hours. Exterior Basic: 1–1.5 hours. Exterior Complete: 2–2.5 hours. Full interior and exterior combos run 3–4.5 hours depending on vehicle size and condition.

faqs.question: Can I book interior and exterior together?
faqs.body: Yes — book any interior package and any exterior package together for a full detail. Contact us or note it in your quote request and we'll confirm combined pricing.

faqs.question: How does fleet pricing work?
faqs.body: Fleet accounts booking 3 or more vehicles qualify for volume pricing. We set up a recurring service schedule — weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly — and come to your facility. Call us or submit a quote request with your vehicle count.

faqs.question: Is the ceramic coating applied by the detailing crew?
faqs.body: No — ceramic coating is applied by our certified Capital Upfitters installers separately from the detailing crew. The detailing package preps the surface and the coating appointment is scheduled afterward (often the same or next day). It requires the Exterior Complete package as a prerequisite.

faqs.question: What's the difference between nerf bars and running boards?
faqs.body: Nerf bars are round or oval tubes that run along the rocker panel — they look rugged and provide a small step. Running boards are flat, wider platforms that give significantly more standing surface. Both improve entry and exit from lifted or tall vehicles. Running boards are better for daily use; nerf bars offer a sportier look. We'll help you choose based on how you use the truck.

faqs.question: Do you carry PowerStep automatic running boards?
faqs.body: Yes. We carry and install AMP Research PowerStep, Bestop PowerBoard, and other electric automatic step brands. Power steps deploy automatically when you open the door and retract flush when you close it — giving you a completely clean appearance while driving. They start around $600 installed, depending on your vehicle.

faqs.question: Will they fit my specific truck?
faqs.body: All the running boards and steps we stock are vehicle-specific — engineered for your exact year, make, and model. They mount to existing frame points with no drilling required. Give us your truck details and we'll confirm the perfect fit. Lifted trucks may require specific offset brackets, which we can source.

faqs.question: Do you install powered / electric running boards?
faqs.body: Yes — we install AMP Research PowerStep electric running boards. They deploy automatically when your door opens and retract flush when you close it. Plug-N-Play install on most trucks — no wire cutting required. Pricing starts from $1,799 installed. Call us to confirm fitment for your specific vehicle.

faqs.question: Do I need an alignment after a lift kit?
faqs.body: Yes — any suspension modification that changes the front suspension geometry requires a fresh alignment. We either handle alignment in-house or coordinate with our alignment partner so you're not driving away with a crooked truck.

faqs.question: Will a lift kit affect my warranty?
faqs.body: Lift kits installed by certified professionals using quality parts won't void your powertrain warranty under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act. However, if a lift-related component causes a failure, that component's coverage may be affected. We use quality branded kits (ReadyLIFT, Rough Country, BDS) to minimize this risk.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a leveling kit and a lift kit?
faqs.body: A leveling kit only raises the front end to match the rear height — typically 1.5″–3″ of lift. A lift kit raises the entire vehicle, front and rear, for true additional ground clearance. Leveling kits are simpler, cheaper, and faster to install. Lift kits offer more capability but require more parts and labor.

faqs.question: Can I fit 35″ tires with a leveling kit?
faqs.body: Usually no — leveling kits typically allow 33″ tires on full-size trucks. For 35s, you generally need 3″–4″ of lift (or more on some trucks). We'll confirm what your specific truck can fit at each lift level before you commit.

faqs.question: Will a tonneau cover fit my truck?
faqs.body: Tonneau covers are available for virtually all popular truck models — F-150, Silverado, Ram, Tundra, Tacoma, Colorado, Ranger, and more. We carry vehicle-specific covers that use existing mounting points with no drilling required. Tell us your year, make, model, and bed size and we'll confirm availability.

faqs.question: Do tonneau covers improve gas mileage?
faqs.body: Yes. An open truck bed acts like a parachute at highway speeds. A tonneau cover reduces that aerodynamic drag, with independent tests showing 2–5% improvements in fuel economy. Hard and retractable covers tend to outperform soft covers in this regard since they create a completely sealed surface.

faqs.question: Can I use the full bed with a tonneau cover?
faqs.body: It depends on the cover type. Folding covers (soft and hard) fold toward the cab giving full access to the rear portion, or push completely forward for total bed access. Roll-up and retractable covers roll/retract to the cab end when fully opened. If you regularly haul tall or long cargo, a folding cover typically works best.

faqs.question: Can I use a toolbox with a tonneau cover?
faqs.body: It depends on the combination. Low-profile crossover boxes work with most soft tonneau covers. DECKED drawer systems are compatible with most hard-fold and retractable covers. Let us know what you have — we'll confirm compatibility before ordering.

faqs.question: Will a toolbox work with my bedliner?
faqs.body: Yes — toolboxes install on top of your bed rails, so a spray-on bedliner underneath is no issue. In fact, we recommend getting the liner first, then the toolbox.

faqs.question: Do you install DECKED systems?
faqs.body: Yes — we're an authorized DECKED installer. DECKED drawer systems are vehicle-specific and require proper installation for the drawers to seal and slide correctly. We handle the full install.

faqs.question: What's the most secure toolbox option?
faqs.body: CamLocker and UWS boxes both use high-quality rotary locks with stainless hardware. For maximum security, add a bed-mounted deadbolt or ask us about cable lock options.

faqs.question: When's the best time to undercoat?
faqs.body: The best time is when the vehicle is new, before any salt exposure — ideally before the first winter. If the vehicle is used, undercoating is still effective as long as the rust hasn't progressed to structural damage. We do undercoating year-round — fall and spring are popular, but any time works.

faqs.question: Rubberized vs. oil-based — which is better?
faqs.body: Both serve different purposes and work best together. Rubberized undercoating is ideal for flat exposed surfaces — it creates a thick, permanent rubber barrier. Oil-based (fluid film) penetrates into seams, crevices, and frame cavities that rubber can't reach. Many customers opt for both for maximum protection. We'll recommend the right approach for your vehicle.

faqs.question: Can you undercoat a vehicle that already has rust?
faqs.body: Yes. For surface and minor pitting rust, we apply a rust neutralizer that converts active rust into a stable compound, then coat over it. More significant rust requires mechanical prep first. We inspect the vehicle and quote any additional prep work before starting — you'll never be surprised by charges.

faqs.question: Is dealer undercoating worth it?
faqs.body: Dealer undercoating is typically a thin spray applied in minutes — it's primarily a profit center for the dealer, not a serious rust protection solution. Professional undercoating from Capital Upfitters uses proper materials, applied with the right equipment, by specialists who do this every day. We see customers regularly who had dealer coating fail within two years. Don't waste the money — do it right.

faqs.question: Is window tinting legal in Maryland?
faqs.body: Maryland allows tinting on all windows EXCEPT the windshield (only the top 5 inches). Front side windows must transmit more than 35% visible light (VLT). Rear side windows and rear window can be any darkness. All our installs comply with Maryland law — we won't install illegal percentages.

faqs.question: How long does window tint installation take?
faqs.body: Standard dyed or carbon film installs typically take 1.5–3 hours depending on vehicle size. Ceramic film takes slightly longer due to precision handling. Most vehicles are ready same-day.

faqs.question: What's the difference between dyed, carbon, and ceramic tint?
faqs.body: Dyed film provides basic privacy and glare reduction. Carbon film adds better heat rejection and a matte appearance that doesn't fade. Ceramic film uses nano-ceramic particles for maximum heat (60%) and UV (99%) rejection without any color or signal interference. Ceramic is significantly more effective in Maryland summers.

faqs.question: Will tint interfere with my GPS, phone signal, or radar detector?
faqs.body: Carbon and ceramic films do not interfere with any electronics. Older metallic films can cause GPS and cell signal issues — we do not install metallic films for this reason.

faqs.question: How long does tint take to cure?
faqs.body: Window tint fully cures in 3–7 days. You may see slight haziness or small water bubbles during this period — this is normal and will disappear as the film cures. Avoid rolling windows down for the first 3 days.

faqs.question: Can I add tint to my ceramic-coated vehicle?
faqs.body: Yes — in fact, our Ceramic Tint + Ceramic Coating bundle is a popular combo. We coordinate both services in the same visit. Tint is applied to glass only; it doesn't affect or interact with paint coating.

aiProfile.brand_voice: Confident, clear and straight-talking. Prioritize accuracy over hype. Speak like an experienced installation adviser: friendly, technical when useful, and never salesy.
aiProfile.target_audience: Truck owners, fleet managers, dealers, and government procurement officers in the DMV (DC / Maryland / Virginia). Mix of consumers and commercial buyers.
aiProfile.warranty_rules: Separate manufacturer product warranties from Capital Upfitters installation labor. Capital installation labor is warranted for six months. Never imply that a manufacturer warranty covers shop labor, and never overstate either warranty.
aiProfile.pricing_rules: Quote ranges only ("from $499", "from $799"). Never give exact prices without a vehicle inspection. Always offer to send a written quote.
aiProfile.image_generation_style: High-quality automotive photography. Crisp lighting, clean shop background or outdoor on-location. No stock-photo gloss. Show real DMV-area trucks/vans.
